data.summary: The gateway directory contains a single Caddyfile that defines the reverse-proxy network edge for the deployment, forwarding incoming requests to the axum backend application and to pluggable web services such as code-server and VNC. It is a pure configuration/infrastructure layer rather than a holder of business logic, and it explicitly documents the deliberate absence of authentication because the trust boundary is the host/LAN.

file_insights.name: Caddyfile
file_insights.summary: Caddy web-server configuration that reverse-proxies incoming traffic to the axum app and to pluggable web services (code-server, VNC) via per-prefix handle_path blocks.
file_insights.source_summary: The file consists of Caddy comments and directives only — no executable code. Comments describe the reverse-proxy design, the extension pattern of adding one `handle_path <prefix>/*` block per new web service before the catch-all, references to design sections §3 / §14B, and the explicit no-auth security boundary.
file_insights.detailed_description: This is the single configuration artifact of the 'gateway' layer (Phase D/G). It defines how the host-facing HTTP entry point routes traffic: prefix-scoped `handle_path <prefix>/*` blocks dispatch to auxiliary web services while a catch-all forwards to the core axum application. It also documents the security model (no authentication, single trusted user on a trusted machine/LAN, D9 design decision), making it both a routing spec and an architectural note.
responsibilities: Reverse-proxy client requests to the axum backend application
Route prefix-based traffic to pluggable web services such as code-server and VNC
Document the extension pattern for adding new web services via additional handle_path blocks
Document the no-authentication security boundary and trusted-host assumption
